subject: mathematics
question_text: If a = 2i − 3j + 5k and b = −i + 4j + 2k, find a × b and a unit vector perpendicular to both a and b.

mark_split.label: Write the unit vector, with both signs

verification.note: Source: Sri Chaitanya, FAST TRACK IPE for Jr. Students — Mathematics-IA (2026-27 edition), book p.72, chapter 7 PRODUCT OF VECTORS, Short Answer question 23(i). Only the question was taken. The solution, the step order and the mark split are this answer book's own work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. THE MARK SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S: the Mathematics-IA volume prints no per-step mark allocation on any answer. The 2+1+1 split gives half the marks to the determinant, because the stem asks for a × b in its own right, and separates the magnitude from the final division so that the ± is written where the student can see it earn a mark. ANSWERS ARE DETERMINATE, not a method sketch: a × b = −26i − 9j + 5k and the unit vectors are ± (−26i − 9j + 5k)/√782. VERIFIED: the cross product dotted with a = (2, −3, 5) gives −52 + 27 + 25 = 0 and dotted with b = (−1, 4, 2) gives 26 − 36 + 10 = 0, so it is perpendicular to both; its squared length is 676 + 81 + 25 = 782, so the squared length of the reported unit vector is 782/782 = 1 exactly. 782 = 2 × 17 × 23 carries no square factor, so √782 does not simplify. BOTH SIGNS ARE ANSWERS: a plane has two unit normals, one on each side, and the card says so on the line the student reads. Paper position: Maths-1A Section B prints eight short answers of which the student writes any six, each worth 4 marks, under the 2026-27 pattern; Product of Vectors supplies at least one of those eight on almost every paper. This is a coaching publication, not a TSBIE document, so the split stays unverified until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

recall_prompt: Say how you would answer both parts — say why the final answer carries two signs.

steps.label: Find a × b
steps.margin_note: Half the marks. Keep a on the second row and b on the third, in the order the stem names them. The j term of the expansion carries its own minus sign.
steps.memory_tip: The j term of a 3 × 3 expansion always carries a minus of its own — write it before working out the bracket.

recall.must_convey: That a × b = −26i − 9j + 5k, from the determinant with a on the upper row.

steps.why: The cross product of two vectors is perpendicular to both of them, so this single determinant answers the first part and prepares the second. Row order matters: swapping a and b reverses every sign.
common_mistakes: Dropping the minus in front of the j term.
Putting b on the upper row, which negates the answer.

steps.label: Find |a × b|
steps.margin_note: Third mark. Check the cross product first by dotting it with a and with b — both must give 0 — then take the square root of the sum of squares.
steps.memory_tip: Dot the result with both inputs and expect 0 each time before spending a line on the square root.

recall.must_convey: That the cross product checks out perpendicular to both, and its magnitude is √782.

steps.why: The cross product must be perpendicular to both inputs, so both dot products are 0. That is a complete check on the determinant and it costs two lines.
common_mistakes: Adding the components instead of squaring them.
Trying to simplify √782, which has no square factor.

steps.label: Write the unit vector
steps.margin_note: Last mark. Divide the cross product by its own length. Both directions along that line are unit vectors, so the answer carries a ± sign.
steps.memory_tip: A unit vector is the vector over its own length, and BOTH signs are correct — write the ±.
lines: A plane has two sides, so both

recall.must_convey: That dividing a × b by √782 gives ± (−26i − 9j + 5k)/√782, with both signs.
accept: divide the cross product by root seven eight two
the answer is plus or minus minus twenty six i minus nine j plus five k over root seven eight two
both signs are correct because there are two unit normals
plus or minus rendu correct, root seven eight two tho divide
the unit vector is the cross product over its own length

steps.why: Dividing a vector by its own length leaves a vector of length 1 in the same direction. There are two such directions, one on each side of the plane of a and b, so both signs are correct answers.
common_mistakes: Omitting the ± sign and giving only one direction.
Dividing by |a| or by |b| instead of by |a × b|.
